page: Microsoft Azure DC96eds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture and managed through the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. It is built to support scale-up enterprise workloads requiring both substantial CPU concurrency and sufficient memory capacity without entering specialized high-memory tiers.

A notable hardware characteristic of the DC96eds_v6 is its large integrated local storage, supplying 5670 GB across local NVMe solid-state drives. This provides high-throughput, low-latency scratch space directly attached to the physical host, complemented by support for Premium Storage remote disks when persistent storage is required. The system configuration includes no discrete graphics processing units and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

By bundling extensive local NVMe disk capacity with high dedicated CPU core density, this virtual machine yields strong cost efficiency for I/O-intensive pipelines that process massive working sets locally without incurring network storage latency. Primary tradeoffs include the ephemeral nature of the local NVMe storage and the lack of hardware acceleration for machine learning or graphics tasks. The server is well positioned for enterprise database engines, large-scale data transformation workflows, distributed analytics caching layers, and high-concurrency continuous integration build environments.
